searchDocs.title: What is VluxySF?​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF (Vluxy Sound Factory) is a sound library for Roblox that lets you play any sound in your game by its name.  You build your sounds in Studio the way you normally would, with their volume, effects and SoundGroup set up, and put them in one Configuration. The library turns that into a compact list both the server and the clients can read, and builds a fresh Sound whenever you ask for one:  VluxySF.OneShot("DoorCreak", door) -- Plays once from the door, then cleans itself up. local music = VluxySF.Fetch("MainTheme", workspace) music:Play()

searchDocs.title: Why use it?​
searchDocs.content: Fetch by name. No folder walking and no WaitForChild chains. Move your sounds around in Studio as much as you like; your code does not change.SoundGroups from your folder layout. Every top-level group in your sounds Configuration becomes a SoundGroup, with a volume for each and one main volume, ready for a settings menu.Low memory. A Sound only exists while you use it. The rest of your library is a small compressed description: about 30 bytes per sound in a real game.Fast. Starting takes milliseconds even with 10,000 sounds, and fetching a sound costs about as much as creating one by hand.Stays out of your way. A misspelled name, a bad volume, audio that was deleted or a mistake in your sound setup prints a warning and carries on. The library never throws an error into your game code.Ready when it matters. Preload the sounds that must play instantly, and warm the ones that matter for one part of the game.

searchDocs.title: Why not use it?​
searchDocs.content: Names have to be unique across the whole game. Sounds are fetched by name with no folder path, so two sounds cannot share a name. With thousands of sounds, naming takes some discipline.Sounds are fixed once the server starts. You cannot add new sounds or SoundGroups while the game is running. Everything a game can play has to be in your sounds Configuration when the server starts.It manages sounds, not playback. VluxySF gives you a Sound; fades, crossfades and music systems are up to you. Wrapping Sounds shows how to plug in your own class for that.

searchDocs.title: Getting started​
searchDocs.content: Follow these pages in order and you will have sounds playing in a few minutes:  Installation: add the package with Wally.Folder Setup: build your SOUNDS Configuration in Studio.Starting the Library: start it on the server and the client.Fetching Sounds: play your first sound.  After that, each page in the sidebar covers one feature, and the Cookbook has complete examples for common jobs like a volume settings menu or footsteps.  info Upgrading from 2.x? 3.0 renames several functions. The changelog has a table of every old name next to its replacement.

searchDocs.title: Getting help​
searchDocs.content: The API reference documents every function, with its parameters, return values and an example.For questions and bug reports, join the Discord or open an issue on GitHub.  note These docs assume you know Luau and how Roblox replication works: what runs on the server, what runs on the client, and how a ModuleScript is shared between scripts.

searchDocs.title: Setting volumes​
searchDocs.content: -- One group, for example from a settings slider. VluxySF.Groups.SetVolume("MUSIC", 0.55) -- The main volume scales every group. VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(0.8) -- Several groups at once. VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes({ MUSIC = 0.55, SFX = 0.7, })   A volume is a number from 0 to 10. Anything else, or a group name that does not exist, prints a warning and changes nothing.  info Where you set a volume decides who hears it. On a client, a change affects only that player, which is what a settings menu wants. On the server, a change replicates to every player.

searchDocs.title: Reading volumes​
searchDocs.content: GetVolumes and GetMainVolume give you the current values, which is all you need to save a player's settings and load them again:  local saved = { Main = VluxySF.Groups.GetMainVolume(), Groups = VluxySF.Groups.GetVolumes(), -- { MUSIC = 0.55, SFX = 0.7 } }   The Cookbook has a complete settings menu that saves.

searchDocs.title: Getting the SoundGroups​
searchDocs.content: When you need the SoundGroup instances themselves, for example to add your own effect to a whole group:  Function	Gives youGroups.Get(name)	One SoundGroup, or nil Groups.GetAll()	Every SoundGroup, keyed by name Groups.GetMain()	The main SoundGroup Groups.GetNames()	Every group name, in the order they appear under SOUNDS  local sfx = VluxySF.Groups.Get("SFX") if sfx then local reverb = Instance.new("ReverbSoundEffect") reverb.Parent = sfx -- Every SFX sound now has reverb on this client. end   See the Groups API for every function.

searchDocs.title: Warm​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Warm( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Warms sounds by name. A name that is already warmed is skipped. A name that is not in the schema prints a warning. VluxySF.Cache.Warm("BossRoar", "BossStomp")

searchDocs.title: Chill​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Chill( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Chills sounds by name: their kept copies are destroyed. Sounds you already fetched are not affected. A name that is not warmed is ignored. VluxySF.Cache.Chill("BossRoar", "BossStomp")

searchDocs.title: IsWarmed​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.IsWarmed( name: string-- The sound name. ) → boolean-- Whether the sound is warmed. print(VluxySF.Cache.IsWarmed("BossRoar"))

searchDocs.title: GetNames​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.GetNames() → {string}-- A new array of every warmed sound name, sorted. print(VluxySF.Cache.GetNames())

searchDocs.title: From Studio to a schema​
searchDocs.content: When the server calls Startup.InitServer(SOUNDS), the library walks your SOUNDS Configuration once:  Each group Configuration becomes a SoundGroup in SoundService.Each Sound becomes a definition: its name, its group, every property that differs from a new Sound, and its effects. Properties left at their defaults are not stored at all.All definitions are written into one compact block of bytes, the schema. Property names, enum names and sound names are stored once and referred to by number, asset ids are stored as numbers, and most numbers take four bytes.The schema is compressed with a fast compressor, made text-safe, and stored in one attribute on a Configuration named VluxySF_Schema in SoundService. A RemoteFunction named Request sits under it as a fallback.  Your SOUNDS Configuration is then removed. The schema is locked from here on: sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game runs.  Every instance the library creates in SoundService carries an attribute named VluxySF. That is how a client tells the library's SOUNDS SoundGroup or UnattachedSounds holder from an instance of your own that happens to have the same name, so you can keep those if you have them.

searchDocs.title: Getting it to clients​
searchDocs.content: SoundService replicates to every player as they join, so the schema normally arrives with the rest of the game. The client requests nothing from the server, and the server does no work per player.  If a client cannot read the attribute, because it is missing, cut short or damaged (NextGenerationReplication limits how long a script-set string attribute can be), it asks the server for the schema through the Request RemoteFunction instead. The server answers a few requests per player and ignores the rest, so a misbehaving client cannot make it resend the schema over and over.  Startup.InitClient waits for the schema, decompresses it and reads its index of sound names. That takes a few milliseconds even with 10,000 sounds. The attribute is left as it is, so other code on the client can still read it. InitClient then starts the preloads.  The wait is bounded. If the schema and the library's instances have not arrived after 30 seconds, because the server could not start, InitClient prints a warning and returns with sounds off for that player, so the script that called it keeps running.

searchDocs.title: What a fetch does​
searchDocs.content: A definition is only decoded the first time its sound is fetched, then kept. A fetch:  Looks up the name, decoding its definition the first time.Builds a Sound with those properties and effects, or clones it if the sound is warm.Runs your preset.Parents it.  Most of the cost is Roblox creating a Sound with a real asset: tens of microseconds on the client. The library's own share is a few microseconds.  A fetched sound is always stopped and at the start. Playing and TimePosition are playback state, not setup, so they are never compiled into the schema: a Sound in SOUNDS is never playing. The kept copies that preloading and warming hold in SoundService are silent for the same reason, with PlayOnRemove turned off on them and restored on the sounds Fetch hands out.

searchDocs.title: When things go wrong​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF is built to stay out of your game's way. The rule is that nothing the library does at runtime throws an error into your code.  What went wrong	What happensA sound name that does not exist	A warning; Fetch gives a silent blank sound, TryFetch gives nil, OneShot plays nothing Using the library before it has started	A warning the first time; empty or blank results. A blank sound from Fetch still goes to the parent you gave A parent that is not an Instance, or a preset that is not a function	A warning; it is ignored, and the sound goes where an unparented one would A parent that refuses the sound (locked or destroyed)	A warning; the sound goes to UnattachedSounds A volume that is not a number from 0 to 10	A warning; nothing changes A preset or jitter builder given something that is not a number, a parent that is not an Instance, or Range bounds in the wrong order	A warning where the builder was called; the preset does nothing, the jitter gives a fixed value, or the bounds are swapped Conversions given something that is not a Sound or not a definition	A warning; a blank definition or a blank Sound Preload or Cache used on the server	A warning the first time; nothing happens Audio that never loads in a OneShot	The sound is destroyed after 10 seconds, with a warning A OneShot whose parent is destroyed while it plays	Nothing; the sound went with its parent A SOUNDS child that is not a Configuration, or a group name used twice	That part is skipped with a warning; the rest works A sound with a property or effect that cannot be stored	That part is skipped with a warning Your own SOUNDS or UnattachedSounds already in SoundService	Nothing; the library finds its own instances by their VluxySF mark The schema attribute cannot be read on a client	The client asks the server for the schema instead InitServer or InitClient called twice or on the wrong side	A warning; the extra call is ignored Something fails while starting	A warning; sounds stay off, and the script that called Init keeps running. A later Init call says the first one failed The schema never arrives on a client	After 30 seconds, a warning; sounds stay off for that player, and the script keeps running  Every warning starts with [VluxySF], so you can find them in the output while testing.  The only errors that can reach you come from your own code, such as a preset or wrapper function that throws. When a preset throws, the sound it was applied to is destroyed first.

searchDocs.title: The basics​
searchDocs.content: Legend:  ⚙️ = Configuration Instance 📁 = Folder Instance 🔊 = Sound Instance   Example:  SOUNDS⚙️ ← The base Configuration ├─ MUSIC⚙️ ← Becomes the MUSIC SoundGroup │ ├─ mainTheme🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC │ └─ battle🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC └─ SFX⚙️ ← Becomes the SFX SoundGroup ├─ click🔊 ← Grouped to SFX └─ explosion🔊 ← Grouped to SFX   There are only three rules:  Every direct child of SOUNDS is a Configuration with a unique name. Each one becomes a SoundGroup with the same name. A Folder or Sound placed directly under SOUNDS, or a second group with a name already used, is skipped by InitServer with a warning, along with everything inside it.Every Sound goes inside one of those group Configurations. It is assigned to that SoundGroup automatically.Every Sound has a unique name. The name is the key you fetch it with, like VluxySF.Fetch("explosion"). If two sounds share a name, a warning is printed on the server and only the first one is kept.

searchDocs.title: Naming conventions​
searchDocs.content: Instance	Recommended	Required?SoundGroup Configurations	UPPER_CASE	No, any name works Folders	PascalCase	No, any name works Sounds	PascalCase or camelCase	No, but the name must be unique

searchDocs.title: Organizing with folders​
searchDocs.content: Inside a group you can use Folders (📁) however you like. Any other instance that is not a Sound, such as a nested Configuration or a Model, is treated the same way as a Folder.  SOUNDS⚙️ └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ UI📁 │ └─ click🔊 └─ Game📁 └─ explosion🔊   tip The hierarchy inside a group does not affect the library. Sounds are always fetched by name, so you can reorganize your folders at any time without touching your code.

searchDocs.title: Preloading sounds​
searchDocs.content: Tag a Sound, a Folder or a whole group Configuration with VluxySF_Preload to have its sounds downloaded when a client starts, so they play instantly the first time. Preloading explains how it works and what to tag.

searchDocs.title: Configuring sounds​
searchDocs.content: Set up each Sound in Studio exactly how you want it to play.  Properties: Set SoundId, Volume, PlaybackSpeed, and so on directly on the Sound. A fetched sound comes out the way you authored it. Parent, Archivable, attributes, tags, read-only state such as IsPlaying and TimeLength, playback state (Playing and TimePosition: a sound in SOUNDS is never playing, and a fetched sound is always stopped at the start), and deprecated properties such as Pitch, MinDistance, MaxDistance and EmitterSize are not kept.Effects: Add effects such as EqualizerSoundEffect or ReverbSoundEffect as children of the Sound.  note Only SoundEffects are kept. Any other instance parented to a Sound is skipped with a warning.Only one effect of each class is kept per Sound. Extra ones are skipped with a warning.A fetched effect is named after its class, so you can always reach it with sound.EchoSoundEffect, whatever it was called in Studio.A SoundEffect cannot have children. Children are not kept, and a warning is printed.

searchDocs.title: End result​
searchDocs.content: When you are done, your SOUNDS Configuration should look something like this in Studio:    note Keep the SOUNDS Configuration in ServerStorage so it never replicates to clients. InitServer takes the Configuration as an argument, so where exactly it sits is up to you.  Once InitServer has compiled it, the Configuration is detached right away and destroyed shortly after, once the calling thread yields or finishes. Nothing else should read from it after that.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: Your sounds are ready. Continue to Starting the Library.

searchDocs.title: Uniform​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Uniform( center: number,-- The value the jitter varies around. Falls back to 1 when it is not a number. spread: number-- The largest distance from the center. Falls back to 0 when it is not a number. ) → () → number-- Gives a new value when called. Spreads values evenly between center - spread and center + spread. local speed = VluxySF.Jitter.Uniform(1, 0.15) sound1.PlaybackSpeed = speed() -- a random value from 0.85 to 1.15 sound2.PlaybackSpeed = speed() -- another one

searchDocs.title: Range​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Range( min: number,-- The smallest value. Falls back to max when it is not a number. max: number-- The largest value. Falls back to min when it is not a number. ) → () → number-- Gives a new value when called. Spreads values evenly between min and max. When min is above max the two are swapped. local speed = VluxySF.Jitter.Range(0.85, 1.15) sound.PlaybackSpeed = speed()

searchDocs.title: Natural​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Natural( center: number,-- The value the jitter varies around. Falls back to 1 when it is not a number. spread: number-- The largest distance from the center. Falls back to 0 when it is not a number. ) → () → number-- Gives a new value when called. Like Uniform, but values cluster near the center and rarely reach the edges, which sounds more natural for repeated sounds like footsteps. local volume = VluxySF.Jitter.Natural(0.8, 0.1) footstep.Volume = volume()

searchDocs.title: What it costs​
searchDocs.content: Measured in Studio with 10,000 sounds that use real asset ids:  	CostStarting the server	About 90 ms, once, before players join Starting a client	About 10 ms, plus however long the preloads take to download Size of all sound definitions	About 30 to 35 bytes per sound, compressed Fetching a sound on the client	About 10 to 60 µs, mostly Roblox creating the Sound Fetching a sound on the server	About 10 to 15 µs OneShot on the client	About 200 µs, most of it Roblox starting playback of a real asset  A frame at 60 FPS lasts about 16,700 µs, so even a busy moment with dozens of fetches is a small fraction of one.

searchDocs.title: Keeping memory low​
searchDocs.content: In short:  Only preload the sounds that need to play instantly.Fetch a sound when you need it, not ahead of time.Destroy sounds when you are done with them. OneShot does it for you.Compress your audio files before uploading them.

searchDocs.title: Preload only what needs it​
searchDocs.content: Tagging a sound with VluxySF_Preload is easy, but a preloaded sound's audio stays in memory for the whole session, and there is no way to undo it. The more you preload, the more memory every player pays for.  If a sound only has to be ready for a while, like the sounds of one map, warm it instead and chill it when you are done.

searchDocs.title: Fetch late, destroy early​
searchDocs.content: Call Fetch at the moment you need a sound, not when a script starts, and destroy it when you are done. A destroyed sound frees its memory, as long as no other sound with the same SoundId is still around and the audio was not preloaded.

searchDocs.title: Avoid decoding everything​
searchDocs.content: Schema.Get() and Schema.GetDefinitions() decode the definition of every sound and keep them all in memory, about 450 bytes each. That is fine for a debug tool, but not for gameplay code. Use Schema.GetDefinition(name) or Schema.Has(name) for one sound.

searchDocs.title: Compress your audio​
searchDocs.content: Shorter, smaller audio files are the biggest saving of all. Trim silence and lower the bitrate before uploading. It is the most work of these options, and Roblox limits how much audio you can upload each month, so save it for the sounds that matter.

searchDocs.title: When to optimize​
searchDocs.content: When you have a reason to: a memory warning on a device you target, or a polish pass before release. Until then, preload only the sounds that must be instant and let OneShot clean up after itself. The rest can wait.

searchDocs.title: Working with the library​
searchDocs.content: Set sounds up in Studio for their most common use. Then use presets or change properties in code for the small things that differ. If a sound ends up very different from its original, make it a separate sound in Studio, even with the same SoundId.Keep sounds out of game logic. Game code should not wait on a sound or branch on one. Play sounds from the code that already knows what happened.Plan names for scale. Names are the only way to fetch a sound, so they have to be unique across the whole game. A prefix per area, like UI_Click or Boss_Roar, keeps that manageable once you have hundreds of sounds.

searchDocs.title: SoundGroups​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundGroups = {[string]: SoundGroup } Dictionary of SoundGroups from the Schema.

searchDocs.title: SoundDefinitionInstanced​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundDefinitionInstanced = Sound & SoundChildrenInstanced A Sound with SoundEffects parented.

searchDocs.title: SoundChildrenInstanced​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundChildrenInstanced { TremoloSoundEffect: TremoloSoundEffect? ReverbSoundEffect: ReverbSoundEffect? PitchShiftSoundEffect: PitchShiftSoundEffect? FlangeSoundEffect: FlangeSoundEffect? EqualizerSoundEffect: EqualizerSoundEffect? EchoSoundEffect: EchoSoundEffect? DistortionSoundEffect: DistortionSoundEffect? CompressorSoundEffect: CompressorSoundEffect? ChorusSoundEffect: ChorusSoundEffect? } All possible SoundEffects to find within a Sound.

searchDocs.title: SoundSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundSchema { SoundGroupContainer: SoundGroup -- Main SoundGroup for all other SoundGroups. SoundGroups: SoundGroups-- Dictionary of SoundGroups under the Main SoundGroup. UnattachedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Un-Parented Sounds. WarmedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Warmed Sounds. PreloadedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Preloaded Sounds. SoundDefinitions: SoundDefinitions-- Dictionary of SoundDefinitions. PreloadNames: {string}-- Names of the sounds the client preloads on startup. } The Schema for the library that is shared on client and server.

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.Get() → SoundSchema?-- The frozen schema, or nil before the library has started. Returns the full schema. Decodes every definition that has not been decoded yet. local schema = VluxySF.Schema.Get() if schema then print(schema.PreloadNames) end

searchDocs.title: GetDefinitions​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinitions() → SoundDefinitions-- The frozen definitions. Empty before the library has started. Returns every definition, keyed by sound name. Decodes every definition that has not been decoded yet. for name, definition in VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinitions() do print(name, definition.EffectsCount) end

searchDocs.title: GetDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinition( name: string-- The sound name. ) → SoundDefinition?-- The frozen definition, or nil. Returns one definition, decoding it the first time. Prints nothing for a name that is not in the schema; use Has to check first if that matters. local definition = VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition("MySound") if definition then print(definition.Properties.SoundId) end

searchDocs.title: Has​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.Has( name: string-- The sound name. ) → boolean-- Whether a sound has that name. false before the library has started. Checks whether a sound is in the schema, without decoding it and without a warning. if VluxySF.Schema.Has(`VO_{npcName}`) then VluxySF.OneShot(`VO_{npcName}`) end

searchDocs.title: GetNames​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetNames() → {string}-- A new array of every sound name, in the order they were compiled. Empty before the library print(VluxySF.Schema.GetNames()) has started.

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: Fetch is the main function of the library. It always gives you a Sound, so your code never needs a nil check.  local music = VluxySF.Fetch("MainTheme", workspace) music.Volume = 0.3 music:Play() -- Later, when it is no longer needed: music:Destroy()   A fetched Sound is yours: play it, change it, and destroy it when you are done.  If the name is not in your sounds, a warning is printed and you get a silent blank Sound named VluxySF_Blank_Sound, so the rest of your code keeps running.  Effects come along with the sound, named after their class, so you can reach them the same way whatever they were called in Studio:  local explosion = VluxySF.Fetch("Explosion", part) local echo = explosion:FindFirstChild("EchoSoundEffect") if echo then echo.WetLevel = 0.5 end

searchDocs.title: TryFetch​
searchDocs.content: TryFetch is the same as Fetch, but gives you nil instead of a blank sound when the name is not in your sounds. Use it when the name is built at runtime, or when a sound is optional.  local voiceLine = VluxySF.TryFetch(`VO_{npcName}_Greeting`, npc.Head) if voiceLine then voiceLine:Play() end   It still prints a warning for a missing name. To check whether a sound exists without any warning, use VluxySF.Schema.Has(name).

searchDocs.title: OneShot​
searchDocs.content: OneShot is for the sounds you just want to hear: a hit, a click, a footstep. It fetches the sound, turns looping off, plays it and destroys it when it ends.  VluxySF.OneShot("SwordHit", character.HumanoidRootPart)   It returns a function that stops the sound early, in case you need to cut it off:  local stopCharge = VluxySF.OneShot("ChargeUp", character.HumanoidRootPart) -- The player let go before the charge finished. stopCharge()   You never have to wait for a one-shot's audio to load. Roblox holds a played sound until its audio arrives and then plays it from the beginning. A sound whose audio never loads, because it was deleted, moderated or is private, is destroyed after 10 seconds with a warning, so nothing is left behind.  Destroying the parent while a one-shot plays is fine: the sound goes with it, and nothing is reported.  info Sound.Played fires as soon as the sound is played, which can be before its audio has loaded. If your code needs the sound to actually be audible, wait for Sound.Loaded.

searchDocs.title: Choosing a parent​
searchDocs.content: The second argument of every fetch function is the parent. Give it a BasePart or an Attachment to play the sound from that spot in the world:  VluxySF.OneShot("DoorCreak", workspace.Door)   A sound fetched without a parent goes into a Configuration named UnattachedSounds in SoundService, where it plays everywhere at the same volume. It stays there until it is destroyed, so destroy sounds you fetched with Fetch once you are done with them. OneShot does that for you.  A parent that is not an Instance is ignored with a warning, and a parent that refuses the sound (a locked or destroyed Instance) sends it to UnattachedSounds with a warning. Neither throws into your code.

searchDocs.title: Using presets​
searchDocs.content: The third argument is a preset: a function that adjusts the sound before it is parented, for settings you apply over and over. Presets have their own page.  local quiet = VluxySF.Presets.Volume(0.2) VluxySF.OneShot("UIClick", nil, quiet)   Something that is not a function is ignored with a warning. An error thrown inside your own preset is yours and propagates; the sound it was applied to is destroyed first.

searchDocs.title: Before the library has started​
searchDocs.content: Fetching before the library has started does not error. Fetch gives you a blank sound, TryFetch gives you nil and OneShot plays nothing. The blank sound is parented to the parent you gave, so nothing lands in the wrong place, and stays unparented otherwise; the preset is not applied to it. The first time this happens a warning is printed, so you can find the script that needs to wait for the library.

searchDocs.title: 1. Add the package​
searchDocs.content: If your project does not use Wally yet, run wally init in your project directory first.  Then add VluxySF under [dependencies] in your wally.toml:  [package] name = "your_name/your_project" version = "0.1.0" registry = "https://github.com/UpliftGames/wally-index" realm = "shared" [dependencies] VluxySF = "greenviper126/vluxysf@^3"   Run wally install in your project. Wally creates a Packages folder that contains VluxySF.

searchDocs.title: Upgrading from 2.x​
searchDocs.content: 3.0 renames several functions, so code written for 2.x needs small edits. Change the version to @^3, run wally install, then follow the table of renames in the changelog.

searchDocs.title: 2. Sync the package into Studio​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF runs on both the server and the client, so the Packages folder has to be somewhere both can reach. ReplicatedStorage is the usual place.  Add the Packages folder to your Rojo project file:  { "name": "your_project", "tree": { "$className": "DataModel", "ReplicatedStorage": { "$className": "ReplicatedStorage", "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } } } }

searchDocs.title: 3. Require it​
searchDocs.content: With the setup above, you can require the library from any script:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF)   Every example in these docs uses this path. If your Packages folder is somewhere else, change the path to match.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: The library needs sounds to work with. Continue to Folder Setup.

searchDocs.title: Warm and chill​
searchDocs.content: -- The boss fight is about to start. VluxySF.Cache.Warm("BossTheme", "BossRoar", "BossStomp") -- During the fight, fetches clone the warm copies. VluxySF.OneShot("BossRoar", boss.Head) -- The fight is over. VluxySF.Cache.Chill("BossTheme", "BossRoar", "BossStomp")   Chilling only removes the kept copy. Sounds you already fetched keep playing.  The kept copy is silent: it never plays, and PlayOnRemove is off on it so chilling makes no sound. The clones Fetch hands out get the authored PlayOnRemove back.  To check what is warm:  print(VluxySF.Cache.IsWarmed("BossRoar")) -- true or false print(VluxySF.Cache.GetNames()) -- Every warm sound.

searchDocs.title: Warming or preloading?​
searchDocs.content: They solve different problems, and you can use both on the same sound.  	Preloading	WarmingKeeps ready	The downloaded audio	A built Sound Waits for the download	Yes	No Lasts	The whole session	Until you chill it  Keeping a warm Sound also makes Roblox start downloading its audio, but warming does not wait for that. When a sound has to be audible the moment it plays, preload it.  note For simple sounds, cloning a warm copy is about as fast as building a new one. Warming pays off most for sounds with several effects, where building takes more work.

searchDocs.title: AddAsync​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Preload.AddAsync( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Preloads more sounds by name and yields until their audio has loaded. A name that is already preloaded is skipped, and a name that is not in the schema prints a warning. VluxySF.Preload.AddAsync("BossRoar", "BossStomp")

searchDocs.title: Has​
searchDocs.content: </> Preload.Has( name: string-- The sound name. ) → boolean-- Whether the sound is preloaded, or being preloaded. print(VluxySF.Preload.Has("BossRoar"))

searchDocs.title: GetNames​
searchDocs.content: </> Preload.GetNames() → {string}-- A new array of every preloaded sound name, sorted. print(VluxySF.Preload.GetNames())

searchDocs.title: Preloading from Studio​
searchDocs.content: The easiest way is to tag sounds in Studio with VluxySF_Preload:  Tag a Sound to preload that one sound.Tag a Folder or any other container to preload every sound inside it.Tag a group Configuration to preload the whole group.  SOUNDS⚙️ └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ UI📁 ← Tagged: every sound inside preloads │ ├─ Click🔊 │ └─ Hover🔊 └─ Explosion🔊 ← Tagged: only this sound preloads   You can add a tag from the Tags section at the bottom of the Properties window.  Tagged sounds are preloaded by Startup.InitClient.

searchDocs.title: Waiting for preloads​
searchDocs.content: InitClient waits for the tagged sounds to load, for at most its timeout in seconds. The default is 5:  VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(10) -- Waits up to 10 seconds for the tagged sounds.   If the time runs out, a warning is printed and the sounds keep loading in the background.  For the fastest possible start, pass 0. InitClient returns right away, the sounds load in the background, and you can wait for them later where it matters:  VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Other startup work runs while the audio downloads. VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilPreloaded() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are loaded.   WaitUntilPreloaded also takes a timeout and returns false if it ran out first. Startup.IsPreloaded() checks without waiting.

searchDocs.title: Preloading at runtime​
searchDocs.content: Preload more sounds by name whenever you know they are coming up, like when a player enters a new area:  VluxySF.Preload.AddAsync("BossTheme", "BossRoar") -- Yields until their audio is loaded. print(VluxySF.Preload.Has("BossRoar")) -- true print(VluxySF.Preload.GetNames()) -- Every preloaded sound.

searchDocs.title: What to preload​
searchDocs.content: Preload the sounds that must play instantly the first time: UI clicks, the main music, common combat sounds.  warning A preloaded sound stays loaded for the whole session, and there is no way to undo it. Do not preload everything. For sounds that only matter for a while, like one map's ambience, warm them instead and chill them when you are done.  The kept copies live in SoundService.PreloadedSounds and are silent: they never play, whatever the sound was doing in Studio, and PlayOnRemove is off on them.  See Performance and Memory for how much preloading costs.

searchDocs.title: ToDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.ToDefinition( sound: Sound -- The Sound to convert. Anything that is not a Sound warns and gives a blank definition. ) → SoundDefinition-- The definition. Turns a Sound and its SoundEffect children into a SoundDefinition. Only properties that differ from the defaults are kept, plus the name. Playback state (Playing, TimePosition) is never kept. local definition = VluxySF.Conversions.ToDefinition(workspace.MySound) print(definition.Properties.Volume)

searchDocs.title: FromDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.FromDefinition( definition: SoundDefinition-- The definition to build. Anything without a Properties table warns and ) → Sound -- The new Sound. Builds a new, unparented Sound from a SoundDefinition. Effects are parented under their class names. Each effect carries its class name as Name. With no effects, pass an empty Effects table and an EffectsCount of 0. local sound = VluxySF.Conversions.FromDefinition({ Properties = { Name = "MySound", SoundId = "rbxassetid://123456789", Volume = 0.5, }, Effects = { EchoSoundEffect = { Name = "EchoSoundEffect", Delay = 0.5 }, }, EffectsCount = 1, }) sound.Parent = workspace sound:Play() gives a blank Sound.

searchDocs.title: Wrapped<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type Wrapped<T> = VluxySF The library returned by WithWrapper. The same as VluxySF, except that Fetch and TryFetch return the wrapper instead of the Sound.

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.Fetch( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?-- Preset to apply before parenting. ) → Sound -- The new Sound. Creates the Sound with that name. If the name is not in the schema, a warning is printed and a silent blank Sound named VluxySF_Blank_Sound is returned instead, so calling code never has to nil-check. INFO A warmed sound (see Cache) is cloned from its template. A sound fetched without a parent is placed in SoundService.UnattachedSounds. So is one whose parent refused it (a locked or destroyed Instance), with a warning. A parent that is not an Instance, or a preset that is not a function, is warned about and ignored. Called before the library has started, it warns once and returns a blank Sound instead of erroring, so early game code keeps running. The blank is parented to parent when one was given and stays unparented otherwise; the preset is not applied to it. An error thrown by the preset is yours and propagates; the sound it was applied to is destroyed first. local mySound = VluxySF.Fetch("MySound") mySound.Volume = 0.3 local echo = mySound:FindFirstChild("EchoSoundEffect") if echo then echo.WetLevel = 1.3 end mySound:Play()

searchDocs.title: TryFetch​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.TryFetch( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?-- Preset to apply before parenting. ) → Sound? -- The new Sound, or nil. The same as Fetch, but returns nil instead of a blank sound when the name is not in the schema, or when the library has not started yet. Use it for names built at runtime or sounds that may not exist. local voiceLine = VluxySF.TryFetch(`VO_{npcName}`, head) if voiceLine then voiceLine:Play() end

searchDocs.title: OneShot​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.OneShot( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?-- Preset to apply before parenting. ) → () → ()-- Stops and destroys the Sound early. Plays a sound once and cleans it up: builds it, turns looping off, plays it and destroys it when it ends. Returns a function that stops and destroys it early. Nothing has to wait for the audio to load: Roblox holds a played sound until its audio arrives and starts it from the beginning. If the audio has not loaded within 10 seconds (deleted, moderated or private audio never does), a warning is printed and the sound is destroyed. With a name that is not in the schema, or before the library has started, a warning is printed and nothing plays. Destroying the parent while the sound plays is fine: the sound goes with it and nothing is reported. VluxySF.OneShot("Hit", character.HumanoidRootPart) local stop = VluxySF.OneShot("Charge") -- later, if it has to end early: stop() INFO Sound.Played fires and IsPlaying turns true as soon as the sound is played, before its audio has loaded. Code that needs the sound to be audible should wait for Sound.Loaded.

searchDocs.title: WithWrapper​
searchDocs.content: </> VluxySF.WithWrapper( wrap: (Sound ) → T-- Turns a fetched Sound into your wrapper. ) → Wrapped<T>-- The library with wrapping fetch functions. Returns a copy of the library whose Fetch and TryFetch pass every fetched Sound through wrap and return what it returns. Use it to get your own sound class, with methods like fades, out of every fetch. The copy is fully typed: whatever type wrap returns is what Fetch returns. VluxySF itself is not changed, so other scripts and packages that require it still get plain Sounds. TIP Call this once in a module of your own and require that module everywhere. The Wrapping Sounds guide shows the setup. local Sounds = VluxySF.WithWrapper(function(sound) return MySoundClass.new(sound) end) Sounds.Fetch("MySound"):FadeIn(1) INFO Presets still receive the Sound before it is wrapped. Fetch wraps the blank sound it returns for an unknown name. TryFetch returns nil without calling wrap. OneShot is unchanged, since a one-shot cleans itself up. If wrap errors, the fetched Sound is destroyed and the error is passed on, since it comes from your code.

searchDocs.title: InitServer​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Startup.InitServer( soundFolder: Configuration -- The SOUNDS Configuration. ) → () Compiles the SOUNDS Configuration into the schema, publishes it to clients, and destroys the Configuration. DANGER Call this once. The schema is locked after it is built, so sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game runs. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS)

searchDocs.title: InitClient​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.InitClient( timeout: number?-- How long to wait for the preloads, in seconds. Default is 5. 0 does not wait. ) → () Receives the schema from the server, then builds and preloads every sound tagged for preloading. It can be called from ReplicatedFirst, for example to play sounds on a loading screen; it waits for the schema to arrive. If the schema has not arrived after 30 seconds, because the server could not start, it warns and returns with sounds off for this player. The library is ready as soon as the schema is received, so WaitUntilReady and OnReady in other scripts resume then. This call itself yields until the preloads finish or timeout seconds pass, whichever comes first, and warns if it timed out. Pass 0 to not wait at all: the preloads still run in the background, no warning is printed, and you can check on them with IsPreloaded or WaitUntilPreloaded. DANGER Call this once per client. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(4)

searchDocs.title: IsReady​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.IsReady() → boolean-- Whether the library has started on this side. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsReady())

searchDocs.title: WaitUntilReady​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.WaitUntilReady( timeout: number?-- The longest to wait, in seconds. Waits forever when not given. ) → boolean-- true once ready, false if the timeout passed first. Yields until the library has started on this side, or until timeout seconds pass. Returns right away if it already has. VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady() VluxySF.OneShot("MySound") if not VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady(10) then warn("Sounds did not start within 10 seconds") end

searchDocs.title: OnReady​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.OnReady( callback: () → ()-- Runs once the library is ready. ) → () → ()-- Cancels the callback if it has not run yet. Runs the callback once the library has started, without yielding. If it already has, the callback runs in a new thread right away. An error in the callback does not stop startup or other callbacks. VluxySF.Startup.OnReady(function() VluxySF.OneShot("MySound") end) -- This line does not wait.

searchDocs.title: IsPreloaded​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.IsPreloaded() → boolean-- Whether the sounds tagged for preloading have finished loading. Always true on the server print(VluxySF.Startup.IsPreloaded()) once it has started, since the server preloads nothing.

searchDocs.title: WaitUntilPreloaded​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.WaitUntilPreloaded( timeout: number?-- The longest to wait, in seconds. Waits forever when not given. ) → boolean-- true once preloaded, false if the timeout passed first. Yields until the sounds tagged for preloading have finished loading, or until timeout seconds pass. Returns right away if they have. Useful after InitClient(0). VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Do other startup work here. VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilPreloaded()

searchDocs.title: The usual way​
searchDocs.content: Sounds live somewhere both sides can reach, and code finds them by path and clones them:  local sounds = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Sounds") local function playHit(part: BasePart) local hit = sounds:WaitForChild("Combat"):WaitForChild("SwordHit"):Clone() hit.Parent = part hit:Play() hit.Ended:Once(function() hit:Destroy() end) end   It works, and for a small game it is fine. Then the game grows.

searchDocs.title: Where it breaks​
searchDocs.content: Paths are fragile. Move SwordHit into a Swords folder and every script that names the old path breaks, often with an infinite WaitForChild yield instead of an error you can see.  Every sound costs memory all the time. The templates sit in ReplicatedStorage for every player for the whole session, whether or not they ever play.  Volume settings take extra plumbing. For a settings menu, every sound needs the right SoundGroup assigned by hand, and someone has to remember to do it for each new sound.  The same cleanup code everywhere. Every one-shot needs the play-then-destroy dance, and every copy of it is a chance to leak a sound: one that never loads never fires Ended, so it never gets destroyed.  Mistakes break gameplay. A typo in a sound name, or a sound someone deleted, errors in the middle of a combat script and takes the rest of that function with it.

searchDocs.title: What VluxySF does instead​
searchDocs.content: Sounds are fetched by name. Folders are only there to organize your Studio view; the code never mentions them.  VluxySF.OneShot("SwordHit", part)   Reorganize as much as you like. As long as the sound keeps its name, the code keeps working.  Only a small description is stored. When the server starts, every sound is compiled into a compact, compressed description that replicates once: about 30 bytes per sound in a real game. A Sound instance only exists while you are using it.  SoundGroups come from your folder layout. Each top-level group in your sounds becomes a SoundGroup, and every sound inside is assigned to it automatically. A settings menu is a few lines:  VluxySF.Groups.SetVolume("MUSIC", slider.Value)   Cleanup is built in. OneShot plays a sound once and destroys it, including sounds whose audio never loads.  Mistakes become warnings. A misspelled name gives a silent blank sound and a warning that names it. A bad volume is ignored with a warning. Nothing the library does at runtime throws into your code.

searchDocs.title: When to skip it​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF is not the right tool if every sound in your game is placed by hand in the world and never created from code, or if you need to add brand-new sounds while the game is running. The introduction lists its limits.  Ready? Start with Installation.

searchDocs.title: 1. Start the server​
searchDocs.content: In a server script, give the library your SOUNDS Configuration:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS) -- The schema can be used from here on.   InitServer compiles every sound into the schema and publishes it. Clients receive the schema when they join; a client that cannot read it asks the server for it once. Nothing else is requested from the server at runtime.  info InitServer detaches the SOUNDS Configuration right away and destroys it shortly after, once the calling thread yields or finishes. Your Configuration in Studio is not changed. The schema is locked once it is created, so sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game is running.

searchDocs.title: 2. Start the client​
searchDocs.content: In a client script, the setup is very similar:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are preloaded, or 5 seconds pass. -- The schema can be used from here on.   InitClient receives the schema, then preloads the sounds you tagged for preloading.

searchDocs.title: The preload timeout​
searchDocs.content: InitClient takes one optional argument: how many seconds to wait for the preloads. The default is 5.  InitClient() or InitClient(seconds) yields until the preloads finish or the timeout passes, whichever comes first. If it timed out, a warning is printed and the preloads keep going in the background.InitClient(0) does not wait for the preloads at all. No warning is printed. The preloads still run in the background.A negative or invalid timeout prints a warning and the default is used.  Either way, the library is ready as soon as the schema is received, before the preload wait. Other scripts waiting with WaitUntilReady resume at that point, even while InitClient is still waiting for the preloads. Fetching a sound that is still preloading works; Roblox plays it as soon as its audio arrives.  When you do not wait, Startup.IsPreloaded() tells you whether the tagged sounds have finished loading, and Startup.WaitUntilPreloaded() yields until they have:  VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Does not wait for the preloads. -- Do other startup work here. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsPreloaded()) -- true or false VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilPreloaded() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are loaded.   WaitUntilPreloaded returns right away if the preloads are already done. It also takes an optional timeout and returns false if the timeout passed first. On the server, which preloads nothing, both report the preloads as done once InitServer has run.  danger Call InitServer once on the server and InitClient once on each client. A second call prints a warning and is ignored.  info Starting never breaks the script that calls it. If something goes wrong, for example InitServer is given something that is not your SOUNDS Configuration, a warning explains it and sounds stay off: fetches return blank sounds or nil, and nothing else in the library errors. A SOUNDS child that is not a Configuration, or a second group with a name already used, is skipped with a warning and the rest still works. A client waits at most 30 seconds for the schema. If the server could not start, InitClient warns and returns with sounds off for that player instead of holding its script forever.

searchDocs.title: 3. Use it from other scripts​
searchDocs.content: Functions used before the library is ready do not error, but they do nothing useful: each one warns once and returns a blank sound, nil or an empty result. Any script that is not the one that started the library should wait for it first:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady() -- Yields until the library is ready. -- The schema can be used from here on.   WaitUntilReady takes an optional timeout in seconds and returns false if it passed first, so a script never hangs forever if the server failed to start:  if not VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady(15) then warn("Sounds are not available") end   If you do not want your script to yield, use OnReady. It runs the callback once the library is ready, or right away in a new thread if it already is. It returns a function that cancels the callback if it has not run yet:  local cancel = VluxySF.Startup.OnReady(function() VluxySF.OneShot("LoFiBeat1") end) -- This line runs right away.   tip If you are certain your code runs after the schema is loaded, you do not need to wait at all. VluxySF.Startup.IsReady() tells you whether it is ready.  See Startup for every function on this page.

searchDocs.title: Advanced: start it from a module loader​
searchDocs.content: If your game loads its modules in phases, like Init and then Start, you can start VluxySF during Init. Everything that runs on Start or later can then use the schema without waiting.  You have to bring your own module loader for this. This is commonly called a single script architecture.  Server module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS) end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Client module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are preloaded, or 5 seconds pass. end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Any other module:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local MyModule = {} function MyModule.Start() -- The schema can be used here, without WaitUntilReady. end return MyModule   note This only works if your loader finishes every Init before it runs any Start. Sub modules can use the schema too, as long as they run on Start or after. If your loader does not want Init to yield, call InitClient(0) there instead and use WaitUntilPreloaded later where the preloaded sounds matter.

searchDocs.title: Built-in presets​
searchDocs.content: Preset	What it doesVolume(volume)	Sets Volume PlaybackSpeed(speed)	Sets PlaybackSpeed Parent(instance)	Sets the parent NaturalVolumeJitter(center?, spread?)	A slightly different volume each time, usually close to the center NaturalPlaybackJitter(center?, spread?)	A slightly different speed each time, usually close to the center RandomVolumeJitter(center?, spread?)	A volume anywhere in the range, evenly spread RandomPlaybackJitter(center?, spread?)	A speed anywhere in the range, evenly spread Combine(...)	Applies several presets in order  local presets = VluxySF.Presets VluxySF.OneShot("UIClick", nil, presets.Volume(0.4))   See the Presets API for the defaults and an example of each.  A built-in preset never throws. A builder given a bad argument, like Volume("loud") or Parent(nil), warns right where it was called and returns a preset that does nothing, so the sounds that use it still play. Parent with an Instance that refuses the sound by the time it is fetched warns and leaves the sound where the fetch puts an unparented one.

searchDocs.title: Combining presets​
searchDocs.content: Combine merges presets into one. They run in the order you list them.  local presets = VluxySF.Presets local impact = presets.Combine( presets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.8, 0.12), presets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(1, 0.09) ) VluxySF.OneShot("RockImpact", part, impact) VluxySF.OneShot("WoodImpact", part, impact)   A parent passed to the fetch function wins over a parent set by a preset.

searchDocs.title: Making your own​
searchDocs.content: A preset is any function that takes a Sound. When it needs settings, write a function that returns one:  local function startAt(seconds: number): (Sound) -> () return function(sound: Sound) sound.TimePosition = seconds end end VluxySF.OneShot("LongIntro", nil, startAt(2.5))   Keep your own presets in a module and use them next to the built-in ones.  tip Use presets to set properties and other quick, one-time setup. Anything that has to keep running while the sound plays, like a fade, belongs in your own code or a wrapper class.

searchDocs.title: Jitter on its own​
searchDocs.content: The jitter presets are built from VluxySF.Jitter, which you can use directly. A jitter is a function that gives a new value every time you call it.  local stepVolume = VluxySF.Jitter.Natural(0.6, 0.1) local function playFootstep(foot: BasePart) VluxySF.OneShot("Footstep", foot, VluxySF.Presets.Volume(stepVolume())) end   Jitter	ValuesUniform(center, spread)	Anywhere from center - spread to center + spread, evenly spread Natural(center, spread)	Same range, but mostly close to the center. Sounds more natural for repeated sounds like footsteps Range(min, max)	Anywhere from min to max  Jitter values never go below 0. A builder given something that is not a number warns and falls back to a value with no variation; Range with its bounds reversed swaps them. See the Jitter API for details.

searchDocs.title: Combine​
searchDocs.content: </> Presets.Combine( ...: (Sound ) → ()-- Your Preset Closures to combine. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the combined presets. Combines presets together into 1 reusable preset. INFO Presets are applied in sequence from first to last. An argument that is not a function warns and is left out. local myCombinedPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Combine( VluxySF.Presets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(1, 0.1), VluxySF.Presets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.7, 0.15) ) local myCombinedPreset2 = VluxySF.Presets.Combine( myCombinedPreset, VluxySF.Presets.Parent(workspace.Sounds) ) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myCombinedPreset2) local sound4 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound4", nil, myCombinedPreset2)

searchDocs.title: Parent​
searchDocs.content: </> Presets.Parent( parent: Instance -- The parent to set the sound too. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the preset. Sets the parent of a sound. local myPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Parent(workspace.Sounds) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myPreset)

searchDocs.title: Volume​
searchDocs.content: </> Presets.Volume( volume: number-- The volume to set the sound too. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the preset. Sets the volume of a sound. local myPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Volume(0.1) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myPreset)

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: WithWrapper takes a function that turns a Sound into your class, and returns a copy of the library whose Fetch and TryFetch return your class.  It is fully typed. Whatever type your function returns is what Fetch returns, so autocomplete and --!strict see your class's methods. No casts.It does not change VluxySF. Scripts and packages that require VluxySF directly still get plain Sounds. Only code that uses the wrapped copy gets your class.Everything else is the same. Startup, Schema, Groups, Preload, Cache, Conversions, Presets, Jitter and OneShot are the library's own.

searchDocs.title: 1. Write the wrapper class​
searchDocs.content: The class takes the fetched Sound in its constructor. Export its type so WithWrapper can pass it through.  --!strict -- ReplicatedStorage/Shared/SoundWrapper.luau local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService") local SoundWrapper = {} SoundWrapper.__index = SoundWrapper export type SoundWrapper = typeof(setmetatable( {} :: { Sound: Sound, _tween: Tween?, }, SoundWrapper )) function SoundWrapper.new(sound: Sound): SoundWrapper return setmetatable({ Sound = sound, _tween = nil }, SoundWrapper) end function SoundWrapper.SetLooped(self: SoundWrapper, looped: boolean): SoundWrapper self.Sound.Looped = looped return self end function SoundWrapper.FadeTo(self: SoundWrapper, volume: number, seconds: number): SoundWrapper if self._tween then self._tween:Cancel() end local tween = TweenService:Create(self.Sound, TweenInfo.new(seconds), { Volume = volume }) self._tween = tween tween:Play() return self end function SoundWrapper.FadeIn(self: SoundWrapper, seconds: number): SoundWrapper local volume = self.Sound.Volume self.Sound.Volume = 0 self.Sound:Play() return self:FadeTo(volume, seconds) end function SoundWrapper.Destroy(self: SoundWrapper) if self._tween then self._tween:Cancel() self._tween = nil end self.Sound:Destroy() end return SoundWrapper   caution Clean up what your class starts. A fade that keeps running, or a connection that is never disconnected, outlives the sound. Give the class a Destroy that cancels them and destroys the Sound, and call it instead of Sound:Destroy().

searchDocs.title: 2. Wrap the library once​
searchDocs.content: Make one module that returns the wrapped library. This is the only place WithWrapper is called.  --!strict -- ReplicatedStorage/Shared/Sounds.luau local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local SoundWrapper = require(script.Parent.SoundWrapper) return VluxySF.WithWrapper(SoundWrapper.new)   Roblox runs a module once and hands every script the same result, so the wrapped library is built once and shared by every script on that side.  tip Put this module in ReplicatedStorage so server and client scripts can both require it. With Rojo, that is any folder your project file maps into ReplicatedStorage, for example src/shared.

searchDocs.title: 3. Require it everywhere​
searchDocs.content: Scripts require your Sounds module instead of VluxySF. Starting the library works the same through it.  -- Server script local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local Sounds = require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Sounds) Sounds.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS)   -- Any client script local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Sounds = require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Sounds) Sounds.Startup.WaitUntilReady() local music = Sounds.Fetch("LoFiBeat1", workspace) music:SetLooped(true):FadeIn(2)   See Initialization for where InitServer and InitClient go.

searchDocs.title: What changes and what does not​
searchDocs.content: Wrapped copyFetch	Returns your class. An unknown name still warns, and the blank sound it returns is wrapped too. TryFetch	Returns your class, or nil for an unknown name without calling your function. OneShot	Unchanged. It returns a cleanup function, not a sound. Presets	Run on the Sound before it is wrapped, so existing presets keep working. Parent	Set before wrapping, the same as an unwrapped fetch. Everything else	The library's own Startup, Schema, Groups, Preload, Cache, Conversions, Presets and Jitter.  warning Do not assign to VluxySF.Fetch to get the same effect. The library table is frozen, and replacing a shared module's function would change it for every script and package in the game. WithWrapper gives you a separate copy instead.

searchDocs.title: Footsteps​
searchDocs.content: Plays a step sound that matches the floor, with a little volume and speed variation so a hundred steps in a row still sound natural.  -- LocalScript local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local STEP_SOUNDS: { [Enum.Material]: string } = { [Enum.Material.Wood] = "Step_Wood", [Enum.Material.WoodPlanks] = "Step_Wood", [Enum.Material.Grass] = "Step_Grass", [Enum.Material.Concrete] = "Step_Stone", } -- Built once and reused for every step. local stepPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Combine( VluxySF.Presets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.6, 0.1), VluxySF.Presets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(1, 0.08) ) VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady() local function playStep(foot: BasePart, floor: Enum.Material) VluxySF.OneShot(STEP_SOUNDS[floor] or "Step_Default", foot, stepPreset) end   Natural jitter keeps most steps close to the center value, which sounds more like real steps than an even spread.Footsteps play constantly from the moment a player spawns, so tag their sounds with VluxySF_Preload in Studio. The first step then plays without a gap.

searchDocs.title: Volume settings that save​
searchDocs.content: Sliders for each SoundGroup and the main volume, saved between sessions. The client applies the volumes, so each player hears their own settings. The server owns the saved data: it checks what the client sends, keeps it in memory, and writes it once when the player leaves.  -- Script in ServerScriptService local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("SoundSettings") local getSettings = Instance.new("RemoteFunction") getSettings.Name = "GetSoundSettings" getSettings.Parent = ReplicatedStorage local setSettings = Instance.new("RemoteEvent") setSettings.Name = "SetSoundSettings" setSettings.Parent = ReplicatedStorage local MAX_GROUPS = 32 type Settings = { Main: number, Groups: { [string]: number } } local settingsByPlayer: { [Player]: Settings } = {} local function isVolume(value: any): boolean return type(value) == "number" and value >= 0 and value <= 10 end -- Anything a client sends is checked before it is kept. local function clean(raw: any): Settings? if type(raw) ~= "table" or not isVolume(raw.Main) or type(raw.Groups) ~= "table" then return nil end local groups = {} local count = 0 for name, volume in pairs(raw.Groups) do count += 1 if count > MAX_GROUPS or type(name) ~= "string" or not isVolume(volume) then return nil end groups[name] = volume end return { Main = raw.Main, Groups = groups } end Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player) local success, saved = pcall(store.GetAsync, store, player.UserId) local settings = if success then clean(saved) else nil if settings then settingsByPlayer[player] = settings end end) Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player) local settings = settingsByPlayer[player] settingsByPlayer[player] = nil if settings then pcall(store.SetAsync, store, player.UserId, settings) end end) getSettings.OnServerInvoke = function(player) return settingsByPlayer[player] end setSettings.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, raw) local settings = clean(raw) if settings then settingsByPlayer[player] = settings end end)   -- LocalScript local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local getSettings = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetSoundSettings") :: RemoteFunction local setSettings = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SetSoundSettings") :: RemoteEvent VluxySF.Startup.WaitUntilReady() local saved = getSettings:InvokeServer() if saved then VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(saved.Main) VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(saved.Groups) end -- Connect these to your sliders. Changes are heard right away. local function onGroupSlider(groupName: string, value: number) VluxySF.Groups.SetVolume(groupName, value) end local function onMainSlider(value: number) VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(value) end -- Call this when the settings menu closes, not on every slider move. local function onSettingsClosed() setSettings:FireServer({ Main = VluxySF.Groups.GetMainVolume(), Groups = VluxySF.Groups.GetVolumes(), }) end   Saved settings from an older version of your game are safe to load: a group that was renamed or removed is skipped with a warning.A real game should also save on game:BindToClose, and may want to retry failed DataStore calls.

searchDocs.title: Mute toggle​
searchDocs.content: The main volume scales every group, so muting is one call. Remember the old volume to restore it.  local volumeBeforeMute = 1 local function setMuted(muted: boolean) if muted then volumeBeforeMute = VluxySF.Groups.GetMainVolume() VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(0) else VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(volumeBeforeMute) end end

searchDocs.title: Music that crossfades​
searchDocs.content: A small music player that fades the old track out while the new one fades in. Switching again mid-fade cancels the running fades, so tracks never pile up.  local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService") local FADE = TweenInfo.new(2) local current: Sound? = nil local fades: { Tween } = {} local function fadeTo(sound: Sound, volume: number, onDone: (() -> ())?) local tween = TweenService:Create(sound, FADE, { Volume = volume }) if onDone then tween.Completed:Once(onDone) end table.insert(fades, tween) tween:Play() end local function playMusic(name: string?) for _, tween in fades do tween:Cancel() end table.clear(fades) local old = current if old then fadeTo(old, 0, function() old:Destroy() end) end current = nil if name then local music = VluxySF.Fetch(name, workspace) local volume = music.Volume -- The volume you set in Studio. music.Looped = true music.Volume = 0 music:Play() fadeTo(music, volume) current = music end end playMusic("Lobby_Theme") playMusic("Forest_Theme") -- Crossfades from the lobby theme. playMusic(nil) -- Fades out to silence.   If you want fades on every sound, give your fetches a wrapper class with FadeIn and FadeOut methods instead.

searchDocs.title: Getting a boss fight ready​
searchDocs.content: The boss's sounds only matter during the fight. Warm them when the player gets close to the arena and chill them when the fight is over.  local BOSS_SOUNDS = { "Boss_Theme", "Boss_Roar", "Boss_Stomp", "Boss_Slam" } local function onArenaApproached() VluxySF.Cache.Warm(table.unpack(BOSS_SOUNDS)) end local function onFightStarted(boss: Model) local theme = VluxySF.Fetch("Boss_Theme", workspace) theme.Looped = true theme:Play() VluxySF.OneShot("Boss_Roar", boss:FindFirstChild("Head")) end local function onFightEnded() VluxySF.Cache.Chill(table.unpack(BOSS_SOUNDS)) end   Why warm and not preload: a warm sound is kept on the client with its SoundId, so Roblox starts downloading its audio right away. Warming as the player approaches gives the audio time to arrive before the fight, and chilling lets it all go afterwards. Preloading would keep the boss's audio in memory for the rest of the session, and it has no undo.Warm early, not at the moment the fight starts, so the download has time to finish.Chilling only removes the kept copies. The theme that is already playing keeps playing until you destroy it.

searchDocs.title: Optional voice lines​
searchDocs.content: Not every character has every line recorded. Schema.Has checks for a sound without printing a warning, so missing lines stay quiet.  local function speak(character: Model, line: string) local name = `VO_{character.Name}_{line}` if VluxySF.Schema.Has(name) then VluxySF.OneShot(name, character:FindFirstChild("Head")) end end speak(npc, "Greeting")   Use TryFetch instead when a missing sound is a mistake you want to hear about: it prints a warning and returns nil.

searchDocs.title: Sounds on a loading screen​
searchDocs.content: To play sounds while the rest of your game is still loading, start the library from your loading screen's LocalScript in ReplicatedFirst.  -- LocalScript in ReplicatedFirst local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Packages"):WaitForChild("VluxySF")) -- 0: do not hold the loading screen back for the sounds tagged to preload. VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) local music = VluxySF.Fetch("Loading_Music") music.Looped = true music:Play() -- Starts as soon as its audio arrives. -- When loading is done: -- music:Destroy()   InitClient waits for the library's data to reach the client, so this works however early the script runs. Call it only here; other client scripts use WaitUntilReady.The loading music is not preloaded on purpose: it is only needed for a moment, and a preload would keep it in memory for the whole session.
